editorNote: Issue #4 covers Monday, August 23 through Sunday, August 29, 1982. The desk gives the visual lead to late-summer arcade and console gaming: Tron was an August 1982 arcade release and ColecoVision launch coverage revived several earlier coin-op names as home cartridges. The computer column keeps the Commodore 64 in view because production was reported as reaching full stride in August 1982.
morningLine: This week: Tron lights up the arcade aisle, ColecoVision makes older coin-op cabinets feel new at home, Commodore 64 production hits its August stride, E.T. stays on top at the box office, and Jackson Browne takes the rock-radio No. 1 slot.

lead.headline: Tron Glow Pulls Arcades Into the Computer Age
lead.summary: By the week of August 23, Bally Midway's Tron cabinet gives arcade floors a ready-made computer fantasy: light cycles, grid bugs, an MCP cone, and a movie tie-in that makes the cabinet look like it arrived from inside the machine. At the same time, ColecoVision's August launch-title chatter keeps arcade names such as Venture, Mouse Trap, Lady Bug, and Cosmic Avenger in the home-console conversation.
lead.confidence: August 1982 arcade and console-release context; exact-day cabinet placement not asserted

computerItems.label: Arcades
computerItems.headline: Tron Becomes the Week's Neon Computer Story
computerItems.summary: The cabinet turns movie-computer imagery into four short arcade challenges, making the game room itself feel like a glowing terminal.

computerItems.label: Home computers
computerItems.headline: Commodore 64 Production Reaches August Stride
computerItems.summary: Commodore had shown the 64K machine at January CES, and by August the production story gives retailers a sharper answer to Apple, Atari, TI, TRS-80, and IBM comparisons.

computerItems.label: Consoles
computerItems.headline: ColecoVision Makes Arcade Ports the Counter Pitch
computerItems.summary: The launch-season promise is simple: bring recognizable arcade games home with a look and pace that can be sold across the same counter as cartridges, joysticks, and TV switch boxes.

computerItems.label: Peripherals
computerItems.headline: The Real Home-Computer Bill Is Still the Stack
computerItems.summary: A keyboard price is only the first line. Disk drives, cassette decks, displays, printers, joysticks, modems, and named software keep stretching the family budget.

market.headline: Store Desk: Arcade Names Sell the Living Room
market.summary: The late-August counter pitch is no longer just machine specifications. Retailers can point to arcade familiarity: Tron on location, ColecoVision promising sharper home versions, and a C64 whose production story makes the home computer feel less hypothetical.

curiosity.headline: E.T. Keeps the Weekend Crown
curiosity.summary: For the August 27-29 domestic weekend, E.T. remains No. 1, with An Officer and a Gentleman moving up to No. 2 while Friday the 13th Part 3 slides to third.
